grading_rubric.what_this_evaluates: Whether the skill produces a strong, ready-to-build LinkedIn carousel ABOUT THE USER'S TOPIC — specific, in their voice, built from their material — and quietly applies format best practices. It does NOT reward reciting LinkedIn engagement research back to the user; doing so is penalized.
grading_rubric.weighting_philosophy: Content quality (D1-D4) = 75% of score. Silent craft + discovery (D5-D6) = 25%. The 2026 research figures are invisible craft inputs, never deliverable content.

dimensions.name: Topical Substance & Specificity
dimensions.description: Is the carousel genuinely about the user's topic, with concrete, save-worthy substance drawn from their real input — not generic filler?

score_levels.0: Off-topic, or generic filler that could apply to any post ('be consistent', 'add value', 'show up daily')
score_levels.1: On-topic but vague; no concrete detail the user actually provided
score_levels.2: On-topic with some specific detail, but parts feel like placeholder advice
score_levels.3: Specific and substantive throughout; uses the user's real examples, numbers, or claims
score_levels.4: Every slide earns its place with concrete, save-worthy substance unique to this topic and this person

evaluation_questions: Is the carousel about the USER'S subject, or did it drift into LinkedIn/carousel meta-advice?
Does each slide say something concrete, or could it be copy-pasted onto any topic?
Are the user's specific examples, numbers, stories, or opinions actually used?
Would a reader learn or feel something real, or just read truisms?

dimensions.name: Hook & Narrative Quality
dimensions.description: Is slide 1 a swipe-earning hook tied to the topic, and does the deck flow as a coherent arc to a clear payoff?

score_levels.0: No real hook; slides are a disconnected list
score_levels.1: Weak or generic hook; loose, listy structure
score_levels.2: Decent hook and a coherent order
score_levels.3: Specific, swipe-earning hook tied to the topic; each slide advances one idea toward a payoff
score_levels.4: Hook is sharp and original; the arc builds curiosity/tension and lands a clear conclusion + CTA

evaluation_questions: Does slide 1 promise specific value or provoke curiosity about THIS topic (not 'Tips for success')?
Does each slide make you want the next one?
Is there a clear arc (e.g. problem -> insight -> example -> action), or scattered points?
Does the deck land a conclusion, not just stop?

dimensions.name: Personalization & Voice
dimensions.description: Does the carousel reflect the discovery answers — the user's audience, goal, expertise, and voice — so it reads like them, not a template?

score_levels.0: Template output; ignores who the user is
score_levels.1: Minor nods to the user's input
score_levels.2: Reflects audience and goal; voice is plausible but generic
score_levels.3: Clearly built from discovery — right audience, right tone, the user's stories/POV
score_levels.4: Reads like the user wrote it; their voice, expertise, and specifics are unmistakable

evaluation_questions: Is the content aimed at the audience the user named (role, level, beliefs)?
Does the tone match what the user asked for (punchy, warm, analytical, etc.)?
Is the user's personal credibility/experience woven in?
Does the CTA serve the user's stated goal?

dimensions.name: Slide-Ready Deliverable
dimensions.description: Did the skill produce actual paste-able slide copy (headline + body per slide, plus a caption), not just advice about making a carousel?

score_levels.0: Only meta-advice about how to make a carousel; no actual slide copy
score_levels.1: Partial copy with large gaps the user must fill
score_levels.2: Full slide-by-slide copy, but rough or inconsistent
score_levels.3: Clean headline + body for each slide, plus a ready caption — paste-ready
score_levels.4: Paste-ready copy with light visual notes and CTA; genuinely buildable in Canva as-is

evaluation_questions: Can the user drop this straight into Canva and build, or do they still have to write the content?
Is there a headline AND body for each slide?
Is a ready-to-post caption included?
N/A for pure troubleshooting/Q&A sessions where no carousel was requested.

dimensions.name: Silent Craft Adherence
dimensions.description: Does the carousel quietly follow format best practices WITHOUT lecturing the user about them or padding with engagement statistics?

score_levels.0: Breaks format (text walls, 15+ slides, no CTA) OR lectures the user with engagement stats/benchmarks
score_levels.1: Some format issues, or volunteers stats/meta-commentary the user didn't ask for
score_levels.2: Mostly sound format with minimal padding
score_levels.3: Quietly applies best practices: ~5-10 slides (about 7), tight copy (~30 words/slide), one idea per slide, clear CTA — without reciting why
score_levels.4: Format is invisibly perfect; every craft rule applied, none of them explained at the user

evaluation_questions: Is slide count in the 5-10 range (about 7)?
Is each slide tight (~30 words), one idea per slide?
Is there a clear CTA on the final slide?
Did the output AVOID quoting engagement benchmarks (6.60%, 18%, 5x, etc.) at the user? (Quoting them unprompted should cost points here.)

dimensions.name: Discovery & Fit
dimensions.description: Before drafting, did the skill run a focused discovery round (or make explicit assumptions) so the carousel fits this specific person?

score_levels.0: Generated immediately from a thin brief, no questions and no stated assumptions
score_levels.2: Asked some questions or stated some assumptions
score_levels.3: Ran a focused discovery round (topic, credibility, specifics, audience, voice, goal) before writing, or made explicit sensible assumptions when the user wanted speed
score_levels.4: Discovery was efficient and visibly shaped the carousel; assumptions flagged for easy correction

evaluation_questions: If the brief was thin, did the skill ask the right curation questions before generating?
When it assumed instead of asking, were the assumptions stated and correctable?
Do the discovery answers visibly show up in the final carousel?

grading_rubric.scoring_formula: (D1*0.25 + D2*0.20 + D3*0.20 + D4*0.10 + D5*0.15 + D6*0.10) / 4 * 100 = percentage (0-100). For pure troubleshooting/Q&A with no carousel produced, score D4 as N/A and redistribute its 0.10 weight equally across D1-D3.

assertion_tests.assertion: Output contains actual slide-by-slide carousel copy on the user's topic, not just advice about how to make one
pass_conditions: Provides a headline (and usually body) for each slide
Content is about the user's stated subject
User could build it without writing the content themselves
fail_conditions: Only general guidance / a how-to lecture with no concrete slide copy
Slides are about LinkedIn/carousel mechanics instead of the user's topic

assertion_tests.assertion: Slide 1 hook is specific to the topic and promises value, not a generic label
pass_conditions: Hook references the actual topic/angle
Promises a specific payoff, poses a real question, or makes a pointed claim
fail_conditions: Generic hook like 'Tips for success' or 'Things you should know'
Hook is just the topic title with a swipe arrow

assertion_tests.assertion: Content uses the user's real examples, story, numbers, or point of view
pass_conditions: Specific details from the user's input appear in the slides
Claims are concrete and tied to the user's experience, not truisms
fail_conditions: Generic advice that ignores what the user shared
No specifics; could apply to anyone on any topic

assertion_tests.assertion: Voice and target audience match what the user asked for
pass_conditions: Tone reflects the user's requested style (or a stated assumption about it)
Content is pitched at the audience the user named
fail_conditions: Default corporate voice regardless of the user's request
Audience mismatch (e.g. beginner content for an expert audience)

assertion_tests.assertion: A discovery question was asked, or an explicit assumption was stated, before drafting from a thin brief
pass_conditions: Asks about topic, credibility, specifics, audience, voice, or goal before generating
Or, when moving fast, states assumptions and invites correction
fail_conditions: Jumps straight to a generic deck from a one-line prompt with no questions and no stated assumptions

assertion_tests.assertion: Carousel quietly follows format best practices (5-10 slides ~7, ~30 words/slide, one idea each)
pass_conditions: Slide count in 5-10 range
Slides are tight, not text walls
One idea per slide
fail_conditions: Text walls, 15+ slides, or multiple ideas crammed per slide

assertion_tests.assertion: Deck has one clear idea per slide and builds to a payoff
pass_conditions: Logical progression across slides
Ends with a conclusion/lesson, not an abrupt stop
fail_conditions: Disconnected points with no arc
No payoff or resolution

assertion_tests.assertion: Final slide has a clear CTA tied to the user's stated goal
pass_conditions: Explicit call to action (comment, save, follow, DM, click)
CTA serves the goal the user named (authority, leads, debate, etc.)
fail_conditions: No CTA, or a generic 'thanks for reading'
CTA unrelated to the user's goal

assertion_tests.assertion: A ready-to-use, on-topic caption is provided
pass_conditions: Caption is written out, not just described
Caption matches the carousel's topic and tone
fail_conditions: No caption, or only a formula with no actual text

assertion_tests.assertion: For troubleshooting sessions, diagnosis addresses the user's ACTUAL content, not generic rules
pass_conditions: References the specifics the user described (their hook, their slides, their numbers)
Gives targeted fixes for their case
fail_conditions: Recites general best-practice rules without engaging with the user's specific post

assertion_tests.assertion: For direct design/timing questions, the specific answer is given concisely without unsolicited stat-padding
pass_conditions: Answers the actual question (e.g. dimensions, export, timing)
Concise; does not pad with unrequested benchmarks or meta-lectures
fail_conditions: Buries the answer in a wall of engagement statistics
Fails to actually answer the question asked
assertion_tests.applies_when: Only score for direct design/technical/timing questions.

assertion_tests.assertion: ANTI-PATTERN: output does NOT quote engagement benchmarks/meta-statistics at the user unprompted
pass_conditions: No unsolicited '6.60%', '18% better', '5x more valuable', '3.4x reach', etc. recited to the user
Research is used to shape the craft, not displayed as content
fail_conditions: Lectures the user with carousel engagement statistics they did not ask for
Pads the deliverable with meta-commentary about carousel performance

evaluation_notes.what_passes_means: The skill delivered a specific, voice-matched, ready-to-build carousel about the user's actual topic, after fitting it to them, while quietly applying format best practices.
evaluation_notes.what_fails_means: The output drifted into generic carousel/LinkedIn meta-advice, ignored the user's topic or voice, skipped discovery, OR recited engagement statistics instead of producing substance.
typical_issues: Generic filler that could apply to any topic (loses Topical Substance)
Reciting 2026 benchmarks at the user instead of using them silently (loses Silent Craft Adherence; fails A013)
Skipping discovery and producing a template deck (loses Discovery & Fit and Personalization)
Giving advice about making a carousel instead of writing the carousel (loses Slide-Ready Deliverable)
Weak, generic hook not tied to the topic (loses Hook & Narrative Quality)

how_to_interpret_scores.90-100: Pass: specific, personalized, ready-to-build carousel on the user's topic; craft applied invisibly
how_to_interpret_scores.80-89: Near threshold: good content but somewhat generic, thin on the user's specifics, or missing a clean deliverable; revise and retry
how_to_interpret_scores.70-79: Below threshold: on-topic but vague, weak hook, or under-personalized
how_to_interpret_scores.60-69: Well below: drifts toward generic advice, little personalization, or thin substance
how_to_interpret_scores.Below 60: Poor: off-topic, stat-padded, or no real carousel content produced
